repositories.name: academic-research-skills
repositories.description: Academic Research Skills for Claude Code: research → write → review → revise → finalize
pros: Provides a comprehensive, multi-stage academic research and writing pipeline ranging from initial planning to peer review.
Includes built-in integrity gates, data access level metadata, and reproducibility controls.
cons: The pipeline relies heavily on LLM outputs, which are not byte-reproducible and may require rigorous human oversight.
Complex multi-agent workflows may incur significant token costs and overhead for simple research tasks.
repositories.security_notes: The README does not explicitly document whether arbitrary code execution occurs. API keys are required, as the prerequisites state that ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be exported or set on the first run.

repositories.name: claude-code-infrastructure-showcase
repositories.description: Examples of my Claude Code infrastructure with skill auto-activation, hooks, and agents
pros: Provides production-tested infrastructure that solves the skill auto-activation problem for Claude Code and Codex.
Features a modular skill pattern with progressive disclosure to keep skills under context limits.
cons: Hooks are bash scripts that require macOS, Linux, or WSL2 and will not run in plain cmd or PowerShell on Windows.
Optional Stop hooks and certain scripts like tsc-check.sh require heavy customization for specific project layouts.
repositories.security_notes: Arbitrary code execution is possible because the repository relies on executing custom bash scripts and shell hooks locally within your project environment. API key requirements are documented for optional AI-powered classification supporting Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic providers, though no API key is required by default for regex-based matching.
